49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
50	
51	```xml
52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
55	```
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
60	
61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
62	
63	```
64	         ┌─────────────────┐
65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
66	         └────────┬────────┘
67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
71	```
72	
73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
74	|-------|----------|-----------|
75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
78	
79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## MBB-level Layout Patterns
84	
85	### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)
86	
87	```
88	┌──────────────────────────────────┐
89	│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
90	├──────────────────────────────────┤
91	│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
92	├──────────────────────────────────┤
93	│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
94	│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
95	├──────────────────────────────────┤
96	│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
98	├──────────────────────────────────┤
99	│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
100	└──────────────────────────────────┘
101	```
102	
103	### Strategic Roadmap
104	
105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
106	
107	```
108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
110	```
111	
112	### Benchmarking Matrix
113	
114	Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.
115	
116	### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)
117	
118	Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## Strategic Use of Color
123	
124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
125	
126	| Purpose | Method |
127	|---------|--------|
128	| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
132	
133	**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix
138	
139	| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
140	|----------|-----------------|--------|
141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
142	| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
143	| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
144	| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
145	| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
146	| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Speaker Notes Style
151	
152	### Narrative Tone
153	
154	Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.
155	
156	### Stage Direction Markers
157	
158	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
159	|--------|---------|---------|
160	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
161	| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
162	| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
163	| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
164	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |
165	
166	### Notes Writing Guidelines
167	
168	- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
169	- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
170	- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
171	- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
172	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`
173	
174	### Notes Example
175	
176	```markdown
177	# 03_strategic_path
178	
179	[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.
180	
181	We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]
182	
183	Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
184	[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]
185	
186	Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
187	Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.
188	
189	[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?
190	
191	Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
192	Duration: 3 minutes
193	Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
194	```
195	
196	---
197	
198	## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement
199	
200	### Content Level
201	
202	- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
203	- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
204	- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
205	- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive
206	
207	### Visual Level
208	
209	- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
210	- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
211	- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
212	- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout
213	
214	### Notes Level
215	
216	- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
217	- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
218	- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

1	# Executor Common Guidelines
2	
3	> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Template Adherence Rules
8	
9	If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:
10	
11	| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
12	|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
13	| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
14	| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
15	| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
16	| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
17	| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |
18	
19	### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)
20	
21	Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:
22	
23	```
24	📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
25	🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
26	```
27	
28	- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
29	- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)
34	
35	> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.
36	
37	Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.
38	
39	**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 3. Execution Guidelines
44	
45	- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
46	- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
47	- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
48	- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
49	  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
50	  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
51	- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules
52	
53	### SVG File Naming Convention
54	
55	File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`
56	
57	- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
58	- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
59	- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
60	- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 4. Icon Usage
65	
66	Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)
67	
68	**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:
69	
70	```xml
71	<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
72	```
73	
74	> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.
75	
76	**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`
77	
78	> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.
79	
80	Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 5. Chart Reference
85	
86	When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.
87	
88	**Adaptation rules**:
89	- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
90	- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
91	- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
92	- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline
93	
94	> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`
95	
96	---
97	
98	## 6. Image Handling
99	
100	Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":
101	
102	| Status | Source | Handling |
103	|--------|--------|----------|
104	| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
105	| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
106	| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |
107	
108	**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
109	
110	**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 7. Font Usage
115	
116	Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:
117	
118	| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
119	|------|--------------------|--------------------|
120	| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
121	| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
122	| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
123	| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
128	
129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
134	
135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.
136	
137	**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):
138	
139	| Marker | Purpose |
140	|--------|---------|
141	| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |
143	
144	> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.
145	
146	**Requirements**:
147	
148	- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
149	- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
150	- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory
151	
152	### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files
153	
154	Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.
155	
156	**File naming convention**:
157	
158	- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
159	- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)
160	
161	---
162	
163	## 9. Next Steps After Completion
164	
165	> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.
166	
167	**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):
168	
169	```bash
170	# 1. Split speaker notes
171	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
172	
173	# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
174	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
175	
176	# 3. Export PPTX
177	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
178	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
179	```
180

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

85	
86	When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.
87

89	- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
90	- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
91	- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
92	- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

99

101	
102	| Status | Source | Handling |
103	|--------|--------|----------|
104	| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
105	| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
106	| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
128	
129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
134	
135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.
136

140	|--------|---------|

142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |
143

    <!-- 
    折线图模板

    <defs>
        <!-- 线条渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="lineGrad1" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">

            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#42A5F5;stop-opacity:1" />

            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4CAF50;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#66BB6A;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <!-- 区域填充渐变 -->

            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4CAF50;stop-opacity:0.2" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#4CAF50;stop-opacity:0.05" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <!-- 数据点阴影 -->
        <filter id="dotShadow">
            <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="2"/>
            <feOffset dx="0" dy="1"/>
            <feComponentTransfer>
                <feFuncA type="linear" slope="0.4"/>

                <feMergeNode/>
                <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
            </feMerge>
        </filter>

        <tspan>营收与利润趋势</tspan>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
    <!-- 
    水平条形图模板
    用途: 类别排名、数值对比（适合类别名称较长的场景）
    适用场景: 销售排行榜、品牌认知度、满意度评分
    支持: 8个条形（可调整为5-12个）
    与柱状图区别: 水平展示，更适合排名和类别名较长的数据
    -->
    
    <defs>
        <!-- 条形渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="hbarGrad1" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#2196F3;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#42A5F5;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <linearGradient id="hbarGrad2" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4CAF50;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#66BB6A;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <linearGradient id="hbarGrad3" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#FF9800;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#FFB74D;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
        
        <!-- 阴影 -->
        <filter id="hbarShadow">
            <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="2"/>
            <feOffset dx="1" dy="0"/>
            <feComponentTransfer>
                <feFuncA type="linear" slope="0.2"/>
            </feComponentTransfer>
            <feMerge>
                <feMergeNode/>
                <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
            </feMerge>
        </filter>
    </defs>
    
    <!-- 背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
    
    <!-- 标题 -->
    <text x="60" y="70" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
          font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
        <tspan>品牌认知度排行榜</tspan>
    </text>
    
    <text x="60" y="105" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
          font-size="18" fill="#7F8C8D">
        <tspan>2025年消费者调研报告 · 样本量 N=5,000</tspan>
    </text>
    
    <!-- 图表区域 -->
    <g id="chartArea">
        <!-- X轴网格线 -->
        <line x1="300" y1="140" x2="300" y2="620" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        <line x1="480" y1="140" x2="480" y2="620" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        <line x1="660" y1="140" x2="660" y2="620" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        <line x1="840" y1="140" x2="840" y2="620" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        <line x1="1020" y1="140" x2="1020" y2="620" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        <line x1="1200" y1="140" x2="1200" y2="620" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
        
        <!-- X轴刻度标签 -->
        <text x="300" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="middle">
            <tspan>0%</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="480" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="middle">
            <tspan>20%</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="660" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="middle">
            <tspan>40%</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="840" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="middle">
            <tspan>60%</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="1020" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="middle">
            <tspan>80%</tspan>
        </text>
        <text x="1200" y="650" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#7F8C8D" text-anchor="middle">
            <tspan>100%</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <!-- Y轴基线 -->
        <line x1="300" y1="140" x2="300" y2="620" stroke="#95A5A6" stroke-width="2"/>
        <line x1="300" y1="620" x2="1200" y2="620" stroke="#95A5A6" stroke-width="2"/>
        
        <!-- 条形数据 (条高36px, 间距24px, 总间距60px) -->
        
        <!-- 条形1: 品牌A - 92% (第1名，蓝色) -->
        <text x="290" y="175" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>品牌A (市场领导者)</tspan>
        </text>
        <rect x="300" y="155" width="828" height="36" rx="4" fill="url(#hbarGrad1)" filter="url(#hbarShadow)"/>
        <text x="1138" y="179" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#2C3E50">
            <tspan>92%</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <!-- 条形2: 品牌B - 78% (第2名，蓝色) -->
        <text x="290" y="235" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>品牌B (新锐品牌)</tspan>
        </text>
        <rect x="300" y="215" width="702" height="36" rx="4" fill="url(#hbarGrad1)" filter="url(#hbarShadow)"/>
        <text x="1012" y="239" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#2C3E50">
            <tspan>78%</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <!-- 条形3: 品牌C - 65% (第3名，蓝色) -->
        <text x="290" y="295" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>品牌C (经典品牌)</tspan>
        </text>
        <rect x="300" y="275" width="585" height="36" rx="4" fill="url(#hbarGrad1)" filter="url(#hbarShadow)"/>
        <text x="895" y="299" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#2C3E50">
            <tspan>65%</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <!-- 条形4: 品牌D - 52% (第4名，绿色) -->
        <text x="290" y="355" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>品牌D (区域品牌)</tspan>
        </text>
        <rect x="300" y="335" width="468" height="36" rx="4" fill="url(#hbarGrad2)" filter="url(#hbarShadow)"/>
        <text x="778" y="359" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#2C3E50">
            <tspan>52%</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <!-- 条形5: 品牌E - 45% (第5名，绿色) -->
        <text x="290" y="415" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>品牌E (性价比品牌)</tspan>
        </text>
        <rect x="300" y="395" width="405" height="36" rx="4" fill="url(#hbarGrad2)" filter="url(#hbarShadow)"/>
        <text x="715" y="419" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#2C3E50">
            <tspan>45%</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <!-- 条形6: 品牌F - 38% (第6名，绿色) -->
        <text x="290" y="475" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>品牌F (高端品牌)</tspan>
        </text>
        <rect x="300" y="455" width="342" height="36" rx="4" fill="url(#hbarGrad2)" filter="url(#hbarShadow)"/>
        <text x="652" y="479" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#2C3E50">
            <tspan>38%</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <!-- 条形7: 品牌G - 25% (第7名，橙色) -->
        <text x="290" y="535" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>品牌G (新进入者)</tspan>
        </text>
        <rect x="300" y="515" width="225" height="36" rx="4" fill="url(#hbarGrad3)" filter="url(#hbarShadow)"/>
        <text x="535" y="539" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#2C3E50">
            <tspan>25%</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <!-- 条形8: 其他 - 12% (第8名，橙色) -->
        <text x="290" y="595" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50" text-anchor="end">
            <tspan>其他品牌</tspan>
        </text>
        <rect x="300" y="575" width="108" height="36" rx="4" fill="url(#hbarGrad3)" filter="url(#hbarShadow)"/>
        <text x="418" y="599" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif" 
              font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#2C3E50">
            <tspan>12%</tspan>
        </text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 图例 -->
    <g id="legend">
        <rect x="60" y="660" width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="url(#hbarGrad1)"/>
        <text x="85" y="673" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
            <tspan>高认知度 (≥50%)</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <rect x="240" y="660" width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="url(#hbarGrad2)"/>
        <text x="265" y="673" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
            <tspan>中等认知度 (30-50%)</tspan>
        </text>
        
        <rect x="450" y="660" width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="url(#hbarGrad3)"/>
        <text x="475" y="673" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
              font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
            <tspan>低认知度 (<30%)</tspan>
        </text>
    </g>
    
    <!-- 数据来源 -->
    <text x="1220" y="695" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
          font-size="14" fill="#95A5A6" text-anchor="end">
        <tspan>数据来源: 市场研究部门</tspan>
    </text>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
    <!-- 
    热力图模板
    用途: 矩阵数据可视化、相关性分析
    适用场景: 相关性矩阵、时间热力图、用户行为分析
    支持: 7×7 矩阵格子
    -->
    
    <defs>
        <!-- 热力图色阶（从蓝到红） -->
        <linearGradient id="heatGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#1565C0"/>
            <stop offset="25%" style="stop-color:#42A5F5"/>
            <stop offset="50%" style="stop-color:#FFEB3B"/>
            <stop offset="75%" style="stop-color:#FF9800"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#D32F2F"/>
        </linearGradient>
    </defs>
    
    <!-- 背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
    
    <!-- 标题 -->
    <text x="60" y="55" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
          font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
        <tspan>用户活跃度热力图</tspan>
    </text>
    
    <text x="60" y="90" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
          font-size="18" fill="#7F8C8D">
        <tspan>按星期和时段统计 · 数值代表平均在线用户数（千人）</tspan>

    <!-- 热力图区域 -->
    <g id="heatmapArea" transform="translate(180, 130)">

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
    <!-- 
    热力图模板
    用途: 矩阵数据可视化、相关性分析
    适用场景: 相关性矩阵、时间热力图、用户行为分析
    支持: 7×7 矩阵格子
    -->
    
    <defs>
        <!-- 热力图色阶（从蓝到红） -->
        <linearGradient id="heatGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#1565C0"/>
            <stop offset="25%" style="stop-color:#42A5F5"/>
            <stop offset="50%" style="stop-color:#FFEB3B"/>
            <stop offset="75%" style="stop-color:#FF9800"/>
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#D32F2F"/>
        </linearGradient>
    </defs>
    
    <!-- 背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
    
    <!-- 标题 -->
    <text x="60" y="55" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif" 
          font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
        <tspan>用户活跃度热力图</tspan>
    </text>
    
    <text x="60" y="90" font-family="-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif"

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">

      <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>

  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#0D1117"/>

  <!-- Top gradient bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="url(#topGrad)"/>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="60" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
    <tspan>What This Means for Your Technology Strategy in 2025</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Gold divider -->
  <rect x="40" y="90" width="300" height="2" fill="#D4AF37"/>

  <!-- 5 strategic cards -->
  <g transform="translate(40, 120)">
    <!-- Card 1: Python for AI/ML -->
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="560" height="140" rx="8" fill="#1F2937"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="6" height="140" fill="#16A34A"/>
    <text x="24" y="32" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#16A34A" font-weight="bold">
      <tspan>STRATEGIC PRIORITY #1</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="24" y="62" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
      <tspan>Invest in Python for AI/ML Teams</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="24" y="95" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#9CA3AF">
      <tspan>Python is the undisputed leader in AI/ML and data science (31% AI, 28% data science). Build hiring and training strategies around Python-first ecosystems.</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Card 2: TypeScript for Frontend -->
    <rect x="580" y="0" width="560" height="140" rx="8" fill="#1F2937"/>
    <rect x="580" y="0" width="6" height="140" fill="#6366F1"/>
    <text x="604" y="32" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#6366F1" font-weight="bold">
      <tspan>STRATEGIC PRIORITY #2</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="604" y="62" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
      <tspan>TypeScript Is the Future of Frontend</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="604" y="95" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#9CA3AF">
      <tspan>TypeScript dominates UI development (62%) and scores highest in developer satisfaction. Migrate JavaScript codebases to TypeScript for better maintainability and retention.</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Card 3: Rust and Go for Infrastructure -->
    <rect x="0" y="160" width="560" height="140" rx="8" fill="#1F2937"/>
    <rect x="0" y="160" width="6" height="140" fill="#F97316"/>
    <text x="24" y="192" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#F97316" font-weight="bold">
      <tspan>STRATEGIC PRIORITY #3</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="24" y="222" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
      <tspan>Rust and Go Are Growth Plays for Infrastructure</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="24" y="255" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#9CA3AF">
      <tspan>Rust (198 satisfaction) and Go (129, plateaued at 18%) are the languages for modern infrastructure. Invest in upskilling teams in concurrency and systems programming.</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Card 4: PHP and Ruby Declining -->
    <rect x="580" y="160" width="560" height="140" rx="8" fill="#1F2937"/>
    <rect x="580" y="160" width="6" height="140" fill="#DC2626"/>
    <text x="604" y="192" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#DC2626" font-weight="bold">
      <tspan>HIRING WARNING #4</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="604" y="222" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
      <tspan>PHP and Ruby Hiring Pools Are Shrinking</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="604" y="255" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#9CA3AF">
      <tspan>PHP dropped from 30% to 17% (2017-2024); Ruby fell from 10% to 4%. Long-term decline signals shrinking talent pools. Plan for migration or legacy maintenance strategies.</tspan>
    </text>

    <!-- Card 5: Satisfaction Correlates with Type Safety -->
    <rect x="0" y="320" width="1140" height="140" rx="8" fill="#1F2937"/>
    <rect x="0" y="320" width="6" height="140" fill="#D4AF37"/>
    <text x="24" y="352" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#D4AF37" font-weight="bold">
      <tspan>RETENTION STRATEGY #5</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="24" y="382" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
      <tspan>Developer Satisfaction Correlates with Type Safety and Modern Tooling</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="24" y="415" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#9CA3AF">
      <tspan>TypeScript (199) and Rust (198) lead satisfaction scores — both offer type safety and modern tooling. Factor language choice into retention strategy: developers prefer type-safe environments. JavaScript declining in overall usage despite being widely used.</tspan>
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- Bottom summary -->
  <g transform="translate(40, 500)">
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="1200" height="80" rx="8" fill="#1F2937" stroke="#374151" stroke-width="1"/>
    <text x="24" y="30" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
      <tspan>Bottom Line: 2025 technology strategy should prioritize Python for AI/data, TypeScript for frontend, and Rust/Go for infrastructure — while planning migrations away from PHP/Ruby ecosystems.</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="24" y="60" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#9CA3AF">
      <tspan>Source: JetBrains State of Developer Ecosystem 2024 (n=23,262) · CONFIDENTIAL</tspan>
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- Page number -->
  <text x="1220" y="680" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#9CA3AF" text-anchor="end">
    <tspan>6 / 6</tspan>
  </text>
</svg>

# State of Developer Ecosystem 2024: Language Trends, Satisfaction, and Strategic Shifts

[Transition] Today we present the most comprehensive snapshot of the global developer community, based on JetBrains' annual survey of 23,262 developers worldwide covering languages, tools, AI attitudes, and career trends.

This deck moves from "how usage is changing" to "what developers actually prefer" to "what to do about it" — a narrative arc designed to inform your technology strategy and hiring decisions in 2025.

---

# 01_cover

Welcome to the State of Developer Ecosystem 2024. This report is built on responses from 23,262 developers worldwide, making it the most comprehensive view of the programming language landscape available.

Key numbers to set the stage: 20 languages tracked over 8 consecutive years of data. This isn't a snapshot — it's a trend analysis that reveals structural shifts, not just point-in-time popularity.

[Pause] The core story: Python has become the primary language for 35% of developers, overtaking JavaScript in ecosystem importance — even though JavaScript remains the most widely used overall.

---

# 02_language_trends

Let's start with the big picture: 8 years of language usage shifts.

JavaScript peaked at 70% in 2020 — but has declined to 61% today. [Data] That's a 9-point drop from its peak. The dominant language is losing ground.

Python rose from 32% to 57% — [Benchmark] that's nearly a doubling, a +25 percentage point increase over 8 years. The gap between Python and JavaScript has nearly closed.

TypeScript tripled from 12% to 37% — a +25 point increase, matching Python's growth rate. TypeScript is now in the top 5 languages overall.

[Pause] On the declining side: PHP dropped from 30% to 17% — a -13 point decline. Ruby fell from 10% to 4% (not shown in this table but confirmed in the full report). Both are losing ground to newer alternatives in web development.

Go plateaued at 18% after rapid growth from 8% in 2017. Rust continues climbing from effectively zero to 11%.

The takeaway: The top-5 landscape is reshuffling. Python is closing in on JavaScript's overall usage lead, and TypeScript is rising rapidly.

---

# 03_primary_language

Here's the surprising finding: While JavaScript leads in overall usage (61%), Python is now the #1 primary language at 35%.

[Data] 35% of developers say Python is their primary language — more than Java (30%), JavaScript (28%), TypeScript (19%), or SQL (17%).

Why does this matter? Because primary language reflects deep ecosystem commitment, not casual use.

Look at adoption intent: Only 6% plan to adopt Python, 5% TypeScript, 4% Java, 4% SQL. [Pause] Below 6% across the board.

This reveals strong ecosystem lock-in. Developers invest years learning a language's frameworks, libraries, and patterns — and rarely switch.

[Scan Room] Strategic implication: When building teams, focus on existing language strengths rather than betting on major migrations. The talent pool for a given language is relatively sticky.

---

# 04_developer_satisfaction

Now let's look at what developers actually love — not just what they use.

TypeScript and Rust are nearly tied at 199 vs 198. [Benchmark] TypeScript edges Rust by just 1 point — essentially statistically identical.

Python follows at 151, Go at 129, Lua at 118. C++ and Kotlin tie at 113, Shell scores 100, Dart reaches 93, and C rounds out the top 10 at 86.

[Pause] The pattern is clear: Type-safe, modern-tooling languages dominate the top spots. TypeScript and Rust both offer type safety and modern developer experience. Python's strength is in its ecosystem for AI/ML.

[Data contextualization] The gap between TypeScript (199) and Shell (100) is nearly 2x — developers don't just "like" type-safe languages, they love them significantly more.

Strategic implication: If retention is a priority, type-safe languages with modern tooling correlate with developer happiness. Investing in TypeScript or Rust may reduce turnover.

---

# 05_domain_specialization

Here's the key insight for hiring and team composition: Each language owns a domain.

Python leads AI/ML with 31% — dominant in data science, ML frameworks, and the broader AI ecosystem. Python also leads Data Science (28%) and Data Processing (17%).

TypeScript owns User Interface development at 62% — React, Vue, Angular, and modern web frameworks are TypeScript-first.

Java leads APIs and backend services at 49%, and application logic at 55% — the enterprise Spring ecosystem remains strong.

C++ leads system tools and components at 27% — performance-critical work, hardware interfacing, rendering.

[Pause] The insight: Language choice is driven by domain, not general preference. You don't choose a language because it's popular — you choose it because it's the right tool for the problem domain.

[Scan Room] For team building: Match language to domain. AI/ML teams should be Python-first. Frontend teams should be TypeScript-first. Backend enterprise work still runs on Java.

---

# 06_strategic_takeaways

Let's translate this into action for 2025.

[Strategic Priority 1] Invest in Python for AI/ML teams — it is the undisputed leader at 31% for AI/ML and 28% for data science. Build your hiring and training strategies around Python-first ecosystems.

[Strategic Priority 2] TypeScript is the future of frontend — 62% of UI development uses TypeScript, and it has the highest developer satisfaction score. If you're still running plain JavaScript in frontend, plan the migration now.

[Strategic Priority 3] Rust and Go are growth plays for infrastructure — Rust has near-top satisfaction (198), Go is stable at 18% after rapid growth. These are the languages for modern infrastructure: microservices, cloud-native tooling, systems programming.

[Hiring Warning 4] PHP and Ruby hiring pools are shrinking — PHP dropped from 30% to 17%, Ruby from 10% to 4%. If you have legacy PHP or Ruby systems, plan for maintenance challenges and eventual migration.

[Retention Strategy 5] Developer satisfaction correlates with type safety and modern tooling — TypeScript and Rust lead satisfaction. Factor language choice into retention strategy.

[Bottom Line] 2025 technology strategy: Prioritize Python for AI/data, TypeScript for frontend, Rust/Go for infrastructure — while planning migrations away from PHP/Ruby ecosystems.

Key points: (1) Python is now primary language #1, driven by AI/ML dominance (2) TypeScript and Rust lead satisfaction — type safety matters (3) Each language owns a domain — match language to domain (4) PHP and Ruby are in long-term decline (5) Ecosystem lock-in is strong — below 6% adoption intent

Duration: 15-20 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip the decline languages section and focus on strategic priorities 1-3]
